question: Suppose Rammohan has kept a cylindrical bar magnet along the axis of a circular solenoid. Now, he is rotating the magnet about the axis of the solenoid. The induced electric current in the coil will be:

options.text: proportional to the number of turns in the solenoid
proportional to the length of the solenoid
inversely proportional to the resistance of the solenoid

solution:
The correct answer is__** Zero**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rotating the magnet about its own axi**s, while it is aligned with the solenoid's axis, does not change the magnetic flux through the solenoid.
 
• This is **because the orientation of the magnetic field** lines relative to the solenoid does not change only the magnet is being spun around its axis. 
 
• The **magnetic field strength and direction at any point in the solenoid remain constant (Zero) during the rotation of the magnet.**
 
• If the magnet were moved differently or oriented differently, you would get a varying magnetic flux and an induced current.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Solenoid

 
 
• A solenoid is an instrument consists of copper coiling over a cylinder designed to create a strong magnetic field inside the coil because of the flow of current through the coil.
 
• By wrapping the same wire many times around a cylinder, the magnetic field due to the flow of current can become quite strong.
 
• Hence we can say that the strength of the magnetic field will change as a current through coil or number of turn’s changes.
 
• Magnetic field strength is independent of the diameter of the cylinder of a solenoid.
 
• Strength of the magnetic field in a solenoid will be directly proportional to the number of turns and amount of current flowing through a wire and will be inversely proportional to its length.
 
• Thus it is given by B = frac{{{mu ₀}NI}}{l}
